facts.statement: Montsecosuchus is an extinct genus of crocodylomorphs.
The genus Montsecosuchus was described by Buscalioni and Sanz in 1990.
The type species of the genus is Montsecosuchus depereti.
The type species was originally named Alligatorium depereti by Vidal in 1915.
Montsecosuchus lived during the Early Cretaceous period.
The original species was described in 1915 from fossils found in the Montsec Lithographic Limestone quarry in Spain.
facts.quote: described in 1915 from the Montsec Lithographic Limestone quarry of Spain

facts.statement: Fossils of Montsecosuchus date to the Upper Berriasian to Lower Valanginian stages.
The holotype specimen, MGB 512, is a nearly complete articulated skeleton housed in the Museu de Ciències Naturals de Barcelona.
facts.quote: holotype specimen MGB 512, a nearly complete articulated skeleton embedded in a limestone matrix now housed in the Museu de Ciències Naturals de Barcelona

facts.statement: The skull of Montsecosuchus depereti was less than half the length of its presacral vertebrae.
facts.quote: skull of A. depereti was shorter in relation to body length than any other species of Alligatorium (being less than half of the presacral length)

facts.statement: Montsecosuchus shares the trait of having three sacral vertebrae with the genus Alligatorellus.
facts.quote: Both Montsecosuchus and Alligatorellus possess three sacral vertebrae

facts.statement: A notably short radius is a unique characteristic of the genus Montsecosuchus.
facts.quote: The shortness of the radius is an autapomorphy of the genus

facts.statement: Montsecosuchus lived between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago during the Barremian stage.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Montsecosuchus belongs to the Neosuchia clade.
